questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop arguing with colleagues at work in a polite way
How to ask for directions politely in a foreign city
How gestures and showing feelings differ between cultures
Why British people rarely argue in public places
questions.why: They discuss gestures, faux pas and how people from other cultures can misunderstand behaviour.

questions.q: What happened between Neil and Tim before the show?
options: They had an argument, but they are still friends
They got lost on the way to the studio
They argued and stopped speaking
Tim offended a guest
questions.why: They had an argument, but Neil asks 'no hard feelings?' and Tim says 'None'.

questions.q: What kind of things do Neil and Tim often fall out over?
options: How much money each of them is paid for the show
Politics and the news stories of the week
Which country to visit for their next holiday
Who presents the show or picks the quiz question
questions.why: They mention silly things like who introduces the show or chooses the quiz question.

questions.q: What does Neil notice about Tim when he argues?
options: He speaks very quietly
He waves his arms around a lot
He shakes his head
He refuses to look at people
questions.why: Neil says Tim waves his arms around a lot when arguing, which 'isn't very British'.

questions.q: Which everyday gesture does Tim say might offend people from the Middle East?
options: Shaking your head
Waving goodbye
Nodding
The thumbs-up sign
questions.why: Tim says our everyday use of the thumbs-up signal might offend people from the Middle East.

questions.q: What did Erin Meyer think was happening in Dubai?
options: Her student had crashed the car
Her student and a man were having a big fight
The man was trying to sell cloth
Her student was lost and asking for help
questions.why: She thought 'they're having a huge fight' and even that he might hit her student.

options: The man was giving directions to Erin's hotel
The man was complaining about the traffic
The student was buying cloth from the man
They were old friends saying hello
questions.why: The student said, 'we weren't fighting, he was giving me directions to your hotel'.

questions.q: Why does Erin Meyer tell this story?
options: To warn people about driving in Dubai during rush hour
To show that her students are good and careful drivers
To show emotion can be mistaken for anger in other cultures
To explain why she got lost on her first visit abroad
questions.why: She says it shows how someone from another culture may misunderstand being expressive as a fight.
